title: Statutory deadlines and rules are labelled '(my guess)' in the brief, with no citation
expected: A rule the playbook or research knows (180-day protest, 24 h before lading, 30-day invoice, 45 days from termination) shows as a rule with its citation
got: 23/24 freight briefs carry '(my guess)'; 2/24 cite any rule. Rules are slots that only the person's words can confirm, so sourced law reads as Athena's guess
suggested_acceptance: A rule slot filled from the playbook or a research lane renders 'rule: <text> (<citation>)'; every freight brief names at least one deadline with its CFR/U.S.C. section; '(my guess)' appears only on facts about the person

title: Value figures carry no source on the catalogue, the Value tile or 'Worth $X'
expected: Each value says author's estimate or measured on invented data, with its basis one line away
got: '$30,000 a year, for the persona' and the catalogue cell with no source; economics.basis is not parsed by the desktop
suggested_acceptance: Every value rendering carries a source word (estimate or invented data) and the basis is reachable from the tile; lib/playbooks.ts parses economics.basis

title: Price-avoided and protection weights are shown as dollars 'Filed on the bench' and 'found in the rehearsal'
expected: Weights (count $1, ISF $5,000 protection, permit and DQ service price avoided) show as counts done right, never with a $ sign
got: denied-party '$10 found' and cards at '$1' each; ISF '$25,000 found' (Lorna); DQ '$540'; oversize '$392.50'
suggested_acceptance: A playbook whose truth weights are not recovered money declares value_kind; the flow, showcase and turn cards render 'N of M right' for it and no $ figure

title: The topic brief's figure disagrees with the flow result on the same page
expected: The brief and the result show the same figure for the same run
got: drawback brief '$13,747' vs result '$11,033' (bench found 3 of 4); lease brief '$1,515' vs '$1,539'; IFTA brief '$56.15 net tax' vs result '$1,845' filed
suggested_acceptance: A test asserts each playbook brief's headline $ equals usd(bench.value_found_usd) or carries an explicit 'of $X held' wording

title: 'Time saved' leaves out the person's review time and hides the sample size
expected: The ratio counts review time and shows its run count; the computed review line is shown
got: Shown 20-99x against 8-63x with review; the 'your review X min' line is computed but never rendered; n=1 or 3 is hidden
suggested_acceptance: The topic tile renders band.athena.line; the speedup divides by bench minutes plus review minutes; the run count shows beside the ratio

title: The interview offers the playbook's invented app names as answer options
expected: Options are real product names for the role, or a generic role label plus free text
got: Ledgerline, Forwarden, Sheafbox, Postwren, Ledgerwren offered in 11/12 chores; 20/24 pairs had to type corrections
suggested_acceptance: No interview option names an invented portal from playbook.apps; an LC re-run shows correction rate under 25%

title: Cards carry 2-4 questions at once
expected: One question per message for a second-language reader (Dario C5)
got: 29/39 cards held more than one question; the prompt allows 4
suggested_acceptance: A plain-reader setting caps questions per card at 1; LC re-run: Dario C5 passes in at least 9/12

title: Items she left alone, and why, are counted but never listed
expected: The topic and the rehearsal list each left-alone item with its reason (J8 DoD, Lorna C7)
got: trapLedger feeds only the 'Traps avoided x/y' count; no chores view lists it; Lorna C7 0 passes, 11/12 not evaluable
suggested_acceptance: grep trapLedger under scenes/chores finds a render that lists action, key and why; the shaped rehearsal lists its own left-alone items

title: Internal vocabulary on every chores screen
expected: No rubric jargon without an explanation on the same screen
got: Catalogue 4 (benched, exceed the bar, bench, edge); topic 6-7 (persona, traps, bench, world, claim, turn, brief); studio 7-8 (lanes, slot, brief, draft, world, rehearsal, card, turn); runs adds ledger row, gate, daemon
suggested_acceptance: A copy test fails on any rubric jargon word in rendered chores strings without a same-screen gloss

title: The 'per quarter' and 'per episode' values sort as if yearly under 'Most value'
expected: IFTA sorts at $4,800 a year (times_per_year 4); an episode value is marked as not comparable
got: annualValue: month x12 and week x52 are clean; quarter falls to the default (x1); episode, run and claim are raw. PER map: year/month/week/run/claim clean, quarter/episode -> 'per X'. For freight, topic.tsx:191 and :246 agree on all three units in use
suggested_acceptance: annualValue multiplies a quarter by 4, or uses times_per_year where given; a test sorts IFTA above a $1,500-a-year chore

title: The catalogue total adds weights and tax credits into '$X found on the bench'
expected: The 'found' total counts only recovered money
got: Freight adds $65,601.51; $25,942.50 (39.5%) is non-money weights (ISF, DQ, oversize, denied); with IFTA credits, $27,787.33 (42.4%)
suggested_acceptance: totals.foundUsd excludes playbooks whose value_kind is not 'recovered'; the totals line names the count of those separately

title: denied-party shows '$0 a year' as its value
expected: A minutes-only chore shows its time value (about 60 h a year per basis), not $0
got: The catalogue cell and Value tile read '$0 a year'
suggested_acceptance: When value_usd is 0, the value cell renders the hours a year from manual_minutes x times_per_year with its source

title: IFTA counts tax-paid credits as value and shows them as 'found'
expected: Value = penalty and interest avoided (R1220, R1230) plus credits a wrong return would lose; never the credits themselves
got: World values the jurisdiction lines at the tax already paid ($1,844.83) while the net due is $56.15; Lorna saw '$1,844.83 found in the rehearsal'
suggested_acceptance: IFTA truth weights the late penalty and interest; the bench found total for a correct return is at most $50 plus interest

title: ISF is valued at two full $5,000 liquidated damages a year and shown as '$25,000 found'
expected: Protection valued at the mitigated figure or as on-time filings, never 'found'
got: The basis itself says a first violation is cancelled for $1,000-2,000; the rehearsal said '$25,000 found' (the judge rated it a blocker)
suggested_acceptance: isf-filings value_usd reflects mitigation, or value_kind is protection; no ISF rehearsal renders a $ found figure

title: The lease escrow is valued at the whole $2,500 escrow per episode
expected: Value = what the chore adds: disputed deductions plus interest ($969.12 in the world)
got: '$2,500 per episode, for the persona'; the world counts the $569.65 the carrier already admits as found
suggested_acceptance: lease value_usd equals the contested amount; the brief carries one reconciled figure

title: Drawback offers only direct tracing; substitution drawback is absent
expected: Steps and rules cover 19 U.S.C. 1313(b) and (j)(2) substitution at the 8-digit HTS level, and the 190.35 notice of intent to export (offline knowledge)
got: Dario has no part-to-kit list; the brief still plans claims 'tied through Larissa's invoice matches' and he fears a weak claim
suggested_acceptance: The playbook names the substitution provisions and a trap for claims with neither tracing nor a substitutable HTS; the brief states which provision each claim uses

title: The brief anchors deadlines wrongly
expected: 45 days from termination (376.12(k)); for non-delivery, nine months after a reasonable time for delivery
got: lease-lorna: '45 days after final settlement (my guess)'; freight-claims-lorna: 'nine months from delivery (my guess)' applied to a pallet that was never delivered
suggested_acceptance: Briefs take the anchor phrase from the playbook's rule text; an LC re-run of both pairs shows the correct anchor

title: Persona and other-chore leaks in the studio

got: The placeholder 'My airline is Skylindle, and I paid with two cards...' shows in every freight chore; IFTA-dario was asked 'file ... with Texas'; customs-dario was offered skewers, grills and knives
